title: Colors and units
summary: Write colours as names, hex, rgb() and hsl(), and choose between px, em, rem and percentages.

quiz.q: Which value is the same colour as `rgb(255, 0, 0)`?
quiz.explain: Hex `#rrggbb` stores red, green and blue as two hex digits each. `ff` is 255, so `#ff0000` is full red and nothing else.

quiz.q: Write a colour using hue 240 (blue), full saturation and 50% lightness.
quiz.explain: `hsl(hue, saturation, lightness)`. Hue is an angle on the colour wheel from 0 to 360, which makes it easy to pick lighter or darker versions.

quiz.q: The parent has `font-size: 20px`. What is the child's font size in px?
quiz.explain: `em` is relative to the parent's font size here, so 2em is 2 times 20px.
`rem` means root em. It always uses the html element's font size (16px by default), so it stays predictable inside nested elements.

exercise.task:
Colour and size the five paragraphs using different notations. Work in `index.html`.

- `.hex`: `color` as the hex value `#ff6600`.
- `.rgb`: `color` as `rgb(0, 128, 0)`.
- `.hsl`: `color` as `hsl(240, 100%, 50%)`.
- `.em`: `font-size: 2em` (its parent is 20px).
- `.rem`: `font-size: 2rem`.
hints: Each class gets its own rule. Colours use `color`, sizes use `font-size`.
Hex starts with # and has six digits. rgb() takes three numbers. hsl() takes a number and two percentages.

checks.name: .hex really uses hex in the source
checks.hint: Write the colour as #ff6600, not as a name.

checks.hint: Write the colour with the hsl() function.
